records.title: StartupBench: Benchmarking General-Purpose Agents on Market-Validated End-to-End Workflows
records.reason: Recent advances in Large Language Models(LLMs) and agents have substantially improved the ability of AI systems to execute complex tasks. records.title: UI-Mate: Advancing Open-Weight Foundation GUI Agents with In-Context Demonstrations
records.reason: Foundation GUI agents can automate complex digital tasks, but deployment is hindered by scarce and biased training data, ambiguous prompts, and unreliable execution. records.title: SkillSentry: Reliable Skill Execution for LLM Agents via Runtime Assurance
records.reason: LLM agents are increasingly equipped with skills to perform complex tasks through multi-step reasoning and tool use. Although skills provide reusable procedural knowledge, agents may still execute them unreliably. records.title: FailForge: Distilling Procedural Competence from Persistent Failures into Code Agents
records.reason: Rejection sampling fine-tuning (RFT) is widely used to train code agents by generating trajectories on verifiable software engineering tasks, retaining those that pass the tests, and fine-tuning on the successful rollouts. However, even strong code agents repeatedly fail on a substantial fraction of such tasks, and standard RFT simply discards these failures. records.title: Active-SWE: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Proactive Bug Fixing without Issue Reports
records.reason: Coding agents powered by large language models (LLMs) are increasingly adopted in software engineering (SWE) scenarios, capable of fixing a specific bug in large-scale codebase.
